subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should the linked PR land as a scoped embedded `sessions_spawn` mitigation while this issue tracks gateway, `sessions_send`/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups, or should maintainers require one shared work-spawning policy seam first?
rationale: The remaining choice is not a mechanical bug fix: it sets fallback-turn delegation policy and decides whether partial embedded protection is acceptable before all work-spawning surfaces are covered.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
options.body: Land or rework the linked PR for embedded `sessions_spawn`, keep this issue open, and explicitly track the remaining gateway, `sessions_send`/cron, and Codex-native surfaces.

options.title: Require Shared Seam First
options.body: Hold the linked PR until one policy boundary can cover OpenClaw tools and Codex-native delegation consistently.

options.title: Split Follow-Ups First
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers create or assign concrete follow-up items for each uncovered delegation surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
recommendation.body: Land or rework the linked PR for embedded `sessions_spawn`, keep this issue open, and explicitly track the remaining gateway, `sessions_send`/cron, and Codex-native surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned on the linked PR and wrote the maintainer-facing cross-harness scope review that defines the unresolved decision.
